blocks.explanation:
A proper fraction whose denominator has an irreducible quadratic factor \(x^2 + 1\) and a linear factor \(x + 3\): Case III.
We must find the constants of the partial fractions.
Plan: write the form, clear denominators to get the identity, put \(x = -3\), compare coefficients, then recombine to check.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{9x - 7}{(x^2 + 1)(x + 3)}\).
To find: its partial fractions.
Method: The top has degree 1 and the bottom degree 3, so the fraction is proper. \(x^2 + 1\) has no real factors (\(x^2 = -1\) is impossible), so it gets a top \(Ax + B\); the linear factor \(x + 3\) gets a constant \(C\) (Case III). We find \(C\) by putting \(x = -3\) and \(A\), \(B\) by comparing coefficients.

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{9x - 7}{(x^2 + 1)(x + 3)}\]
\[= \dfrac{Ax + B}{x^2 + 1} + \dfrac{C}{x + 3}\]
Why: A quadratic factor that cannot be split needs a linear top \(Ax + B\); a linear factor needs only a constant.

Clear the denominators: the identity
\[9x - 7 = (Ax + B)(x + 3)\]
\[+ C(x^2 + 1) \quad \text{(i)}\]
Why: Multiply both sides by \((x^2 + 1)(x + 3)\). Under \(Ax + B\) the factor \(x + 3\) is left; under \(C\) the factor \(x^2 + 1\) is left. (i) is an identity, true for every \(x\).

Put \(x = -3\) in (i) to find \(C\)
\[9(-3) - 7 = 0 + C(9 + 1)\]
\[-34 = 10C\]
\[C = -\dfrac{17}{5}\]
Why: \(x = -3\) makes \(x + 3 = 0\), so the \((Ax + B)\) term vanishes and only \(C\) is left.

Expand the right side of (i)
\[(Ax + B)(x + 3)\]
\[= Ax^2 + 3Ax + Bx + 3B\]
\[C(x^2 + 1) = Cx^2 + C\]
\[9x - 7 = (A + C)x^2\]
\[+ (3A + B)x + (3B + C)\]
Why: To compare coefficients, each power of \(x\) must be collected in one place.

Compare coefficients
\[x^2:\ 0 = A + C\]
\[A = -C = \dfrac{17}{5}\]
\[\text{const}:\ -7 = 3B + C\]
\[3B = -7 + \dfrac{17}{5} = -\dfrac{18}{5}\]
\[B = -\dfrac{6}{5}\]
Why: Two polynomials are identical only if the coefficients of equal powers of \(x\) are equal. The left side has no \(x^2\) term, so its \(x^2\) coefficient is 0.

Test with the \(x\) coefficient
\[3A + B = \dfrac{51}{5} - \dfrac{6}{5}\]
\[= \dfrac{45}{5} = 9 \;\checkmark\]
Why: We did not use this equation to find the constants, so it is an independent test: the left side has \(9x\).

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{Ax + B}{x^2 + 1} = \dfrac{17x - 6}{5(x^2 + 1)}\]
\[\dfrac{C}{x + 3} = -\dfrac{17}{5(x + 3)}\]
Why: \(\frac{17}{5}x - \frac{6}{5} = \frac{17x - 6}{5}\); the 5 moves into the denominator.

Check: recombine
Common denominator \(5(x^2 + 1)(x + 3)\); top:
\[(17x - 6)(x + 3)\]
\[= 17x^2 + 45x - 18\]
\[17(x^2 + 1) = 17x^2 + 17\]
\[\text{Top} = 45x - 35\]
\[= 5(9x - 7) \;\checkmark\]
Why: Over the common denominator \(5(x^2 + 1)(x + 3)\) the top is \(5(9x - 7)\); cancelling the 5 gives back \(\frac{9x - 7}{(x^2 + 1)(x + 3)}\).
